tools.name: list_tools
tools.description: Which APIs the compendium covers, each with the HOSTS its trials hit (match the URL you are about to call), trust tier, version count and verified-claim / divergence counts. Call once per session; then get_tool_docs for the host you are about to call.

tools.name: list_versions
tools.description: Spec versions of one API, newest first, each fingerprinted by its spec hash. Use with get_version_diff when a spec changed and you want to know what changed in BEHAVIOR.

tools.name: get_tool_knowledge
tools.description: Every VERIFIED claim about an API as structured records (latest version by default), paginated, spec divergences flagged, each with compact evidence (trial id, probe, status, request line). Use when you need to filter by kind or process claims programmatically; for the one-read summary before callin

tools.name: get_divergences
tools.description: Where the live API CONTRADICTS its own OpenAPI spec: documented limits not enforced, types not validated, required params not required, enums that accept other values. Read before trusting a spec-generated client or SDK for this API. Compact evidence; verbose=true adds response previews.

tools.name: search_claims
tools.description: Call this when an API call FAILED or behaved unexpectedly: an unexpected 4xx/5xx, a parameter that seems ignored, an odd page, wrong filter results. Full-text search over verified claims with the host and the symptom, e.g. "github per_page 500", "npm search size 0", "is latitude required on /v1/fore

tools.name: get_tool_docs
tools.description: READ THIS BEFORE YOUR FIRST CALL to an API the compendium covers. Pass the host or URL you are about to call (api.github.com, https://registry.npmjs.org/-/v1/search) or the tool name. Returns a Markdown behavior sheet built only from verified claims: where the API contradicts its spec first, then si

tools.name: get_version_diff
tools.description: What changed in verified BEHAVIOR between two spec versions of an API (changed / added / removed claims), as opposed to what changed in the spec text. Version ids come from list_versions.

tools.name: request_target
tools.description: The API you are about to call is NOT covered (not in list_tools)? Ask the compendium to test it. Pass a target object: { name, spec_url (OpenAPI 3 document), category?, include_paths?, baseline? (valid values for required params per path), optional_values?, server? }. Scope: public read-only APIs wi

tools.name: get_request_status
tools.description: Status of a target request: pending | running | done | failed, with the run id and summary once processed.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_tool_knowledge" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.detail: Description of "request_target" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
